title: Chest freezer run as a solar fridge
summary: Plug a working chest freezer into an external thermostat set to 2–5 °C and it becomes a fridge that uses a fraction of the power of an upright one: often 100–400 Wh a day. Run it from a battery bank through a pure-sine inverter, charged by solar panels. Size the bank from what the fridge and the inverter really use (worked example in the notes). Test a salvaged freezer before you rely on it, and stand it upright for at least 4 hours, better a day, after moving it.

materials.item: Chest freezer, 100–250 L, tested working (see steps)
Plug-in thermostat with a probe and a cooling mode, rated 10 A or more, ideally with a compressor restart delay
Pure-sine inverter, 600 W or more continuous, surge 1,200 W or more, idle draw under 15 W
Battery bank: about 200 Ah of 12V deep-cycle lead-acid, or 100–120 Ah of 12.8V lithium iron phosphate (size yours with the notes)
Charge controller rated for the panels (build_solar_12v_system)
Inverter cables: 16–25 mm² (6–4 AWG), 1.5 m or shorter, with crimped lugs
Main fuse or DC breaker, 80–100 A, within 30 cm of battery +
Small jar of water to hold the thermostat probe
Plug-in energy meter, or a clamp meter, to measure what the freezer uses
Wire rack or crates to keep food off the damp floor of the cabinet
Extra insulation for the lid only: foam board or a folded blanket
Low-voltage disconnect, if the inverter's own cut-off is too low for lead-acid

steps.text: Look the freezer over where you find it: chest type, no rust holes in the floor, a lid seal that is soft and whole, hinges that hold the lid up. Look at the pipes by the compressor for oily, dusty patches (a refrigerant leak). Read the label for its refrigerant and its power use.
steps.warn: Don't cut, bend or puncture any pipe. Many newer freezers use isobutane (R600a), which is flammable.

steps.text: Move it upright if at all possible. Tape the lid shut, lift from the base with two people, and never carry it by the lid. If it must lie down, lay it on a long side, never upside down.
steps.warn: A chest freezer weighs 30–60 kg and is awkward. Lift with your legs, with a second person or a trolley (safety_lifting).

steps.text: Stand it upright where it will live, and leave it switched off for at least as long as it lay down: 4 hours minimum, 24 hours to be safe. Running it sooner can pump oil into the pipes and ruin the compressor.
Clean it out: remove old food, open the drain plug, wash with warm water and baking soda, and dry it with the lid open.
steps.warn: Rotten food and mould: wear gloves and a mask, work with the lid open in fresh air, and keep children away from an open freezer.

steps.text: Test it on mains, a generator or your inverter. The compressor should start within a few minutes and hum steadily. Within 15 minutes the outer walls or rear grille feel warm; within 30 minutes the inside walls feel cold; an empty cabinet should read below 0 °C in 2–4 hours and −15 °C or colder by morning.
steps.warn: Mains voltage. Keep plugs and leads dry and off the floor where water collects.

steps.text: If it clicks on and off every minute or so without cooling, hums but never cools, or trips the supply, it is faulty (a start relay can sometimes be swapped; a dead compressor can't be fixed in the field). Find another.

Set up the thermostat: plug it into the power, plug the freezer into it, and turn the freezer's own dial to its coldest. Put the probe in the small jar of water, hanging halfway down the cabinet, not touching a wall. Run the thin probe cable under the lid seal.
steps.warn: Never drill or screw into a freezer's walls, floor or lid: refrigerant pipes run inside them.

steps.text: Program it: cooling mode, compressor on at 5 °C and off at 2 °C (a setpoint of about 3 °C with a 2–3 °C gap), and a restart delay of 3–5 minutes if it has one. Check with the fridge thermometer at the bottom (the coldest place) and the top.

Measure what it uses: run it for 24 hours as a fridge on a plug-in energy meter, with some food or water bottles inside. No meter: clamp the running current, multiply by mains voltage, and time how many minutes per hour it runs.
Size the battery and panels from your measurement and the inverter's idle draw using the worked example in the notes. Build the panel, controller and battery side as in build_solar_12v_system.
Wire the inverter close to the battery with short heavy cables and the main fuse within 30 cm of battery +. Leave the fuse out until everything else is connected, then fit it.
steps.warn: Remove rings and watches. A spanner across battery terminals welds and burns. Keep lead-acid batteries ventilated: charging gives off explosive hydrogen (safety_lead_acid).

steps.text: Plug the thermostat into the inverter and check the compressor starts every time. If the inverter beeps, trips or the lights dim hard at start-up, the inverter is too small, the cables too thin, or the battery too flat.

Run it well: load it with food that is already cold, keep it fairly full (add water bottles), open it briefly, and check the thermometer each morning. Wipe out water that collects at the bottom each week. Keep it in shade with 10 cm of air round the sides.

notes:
## How it works
A freezer's own thermostat won't go above about −10 °C. The external thermostat sits between the plug and the freezer and simply switches the whole freezer on below about 5 °C and off at about 2 °C. The probe sits in a jar of water so it reads the temperature of the food, not brief gusts of air, which keeps the compressor running in long, efficient cycles.

## Why a chest beats an upright
- Cold air is heavy. Open an upright's door and its cold air pours out on the floor; open a chest's lid and nearly all of it stays put.
- Freezers carry thick insulation built for −18 °C. Run at +4 °C in a 25 °C room, the temperature gap is about half, so heat leaks in at about half the rate, and the compressor works more easily at a warmer setting too.
- No defrost heaters, internal fans or ice makers, which frost-free uprights run all day.
- Typical use: an upright fridge-freezer 1,000–2,000 Wh a day; a chest freezer as a fridge about 100–400 Wh a day in a 20–25 °C room, more in heat or if opened often.

## Sizing the battery bank (worked example)
Use your own measured numbers; these are an example.

1. Fridge, measured at the plug: **300 Wh a day**.
2. Inverter losses (about 85% efficient): 300 ÷ 0.85 = **about 350 Wh** from the battery.
3. Inverter idle draw, on all day because the thermostat needs power: 10 W × 24 h = **240 Wh**. Measure yours: battery current with nothing plugged in × battery voltage.
4. Daily total: 350 + 240 = **about 600 Wh**.
5. Reserve for cloudy days: 2 days × 600 = **1,200 Wh**.
6. Lead-acid, using only half its capacity for a long life: 1,200 ÷ 0.5 = 2,400 Wh. ÷ 12 V = **200 Ah**.
7. Lithium iron phosphate, using about 80%: 1,200 ÷ 0.8 = 1,500 Wh. ÷ 12.8 V = **about 120 Ah**.

Note that the inverter's idle draw is nearly as big as the fridge. An inverter that idles at 25 W uses 600 Wh a day by itself: pick the one with the lowest idle draw that still starts the compressor.

## Sizing the panels
Panels needed ≈ daily Wh ÷ (full-sun hours × 0.7). The 0.7 covers heat, dirt, wiring and charging losses.
- Summer, about 5 sun-hours: 600 ÷ 3.5 = about 170 W.
- Winter or cloudy season, about 2.5 sun-hours: 600 ÷ 1.75 = about 340 W.

So 300–400 W of panels keeps up most of the year, and more lets the bank refill after cloudy days. See reference_power_budget for other loads.

## Inverter and wiring
- **Pure sine.** Compressors on modified-sine inverters run hotter, buzz, and some won't start.
- **Surge.** A compressor draws several times its running power for under a second at start. 600 W continuous with 1,200 W surge starts most chest freezers; small ones often start on less. Test before you rely on it.
- **Cables.** At 12V, 600 W is 50 A and the start surge more than 100 A. Use 16–25 mm² (6–4 AWG), as short as possible, with a fuse at the battery sized to the cable (reference_wire_gauge).
- **Low-voltage cut-off.** Lead-acid should stop at about 12.0V under this kind of load. Many inverters cut out lower: add a battery protector or set it if you can.

## Checking a used freezer
- Running current at the plug: roughly 0.5–1 A at 230V or 1–2 A at 120V. Much more, or a hum with no start, means trouble.
- Most chest freezers shed heat through their outer walls (a skin condenser), so the sides get warm when it runs. That is normal.
- One that sat for months with rotten food usually cleans up. One with oily pipe joints or rusted-through floor pans usually doesn't.

## Moving it
- Upright is best. On its long side is acceptable. Never upside down or on the end with the compressor.
- Stand it upright before running for at least as long as it lay down: 4 hours minimum, 24 hours to be safe. Oil needs time to drain back into the compressor.
- Tape the lid shut and protect the hinges and the pipes round the compressor from knocks.

## Mistakes
- Insulating the side walls: on most chest freezers they are the condenser and must shed heat. Insulate the lid only.
- A probe touching the cold wall or hanging in air: the compressor short-cycles and the food runs warm.
- No restart delay: a compressor restarted against pressure stalls and trips its overload.
- Ignoring inverter idle draw when sizing the bank.
- Thin or long battery cables: the voltage sags at start-up and the inverter trips.
- Putting it in sun, a hot shed or a tight alcove.
- Water pooling at the bottom: wipe it out, or it smells and grows mould.

## Food safety and children
- Keep food at 1–4 °C. Above 5 °C germs grow faster; at 0 °C the bottom freezes.
- Store raw meat at the bottom in closed containers.
- Children can be trapped inside a chest freezer and suffocate. Never leave one where children play, and take the lid off any freezer you abandon.

## Variations
- **12V compressor fridge** (boats, RVs, trucks): runs straight from the battery with no inverter and uses about 250–600 Wh a day. If you find one, use it.
- **Daytime only:** with plenty of water bottles inside as a cold store, run it on a timer only while the sun shines. The bank can be much smaller, but test that it holds temperature overnight.
- **Freezer and fridge pair:** run one freezer as a freezer to freeze water bottles, and swap them into the fridge daily.
